spots.name: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep
spots.summary: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep is a Theravada Buddhist temple (wat) in Chiang Mai Province, Thailand. The temple is often referred to as "Doi Suthep" although this is actually the name of the mountain where it is located. It is a sacred site to many Thai people.

spots.name: Wat Chedi Luang

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Chedi Luang is a Buddhist temple in the historic centre of Chiang Mai, Thailand. The current temple grounds were originally made up of three temples — Wat Chedi Luang, Wat Ho Tham and Wat Sukmin.

spots.name: Wat Phra Singh

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Phra Singh (full name: Wat Phra Singh Woramahaviharn; Northern Thai: ᩅᩢ᩠ᨯᩕᨻᩈᩥᨦ᩠ᩉ᩺ᩅᩴᩬᩁᨾᩉᩣᩅᩥᩉᩣ᩠ᩁ; Thai: วัดพระสิงห์วรมหาวิหาร; RTGS: Wat Phra Sing Wora Maha Wihan; is a Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai, Northern Thailand. It is the place where the image of Phra Buddha Sihing is enshrined.

spots.name: Wat Chet Yot

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Chet Yot or officially called Wat Photharam Maha Wihan is a Buddhist temple (Wat) in Chiang Mai in northern Thailand. It is a centre of pilgrimage for those born in the year of the Snake.

spots.name: Wat Chiang Man
spots.summary: Wat Chiang Man is a Buddhist temple inside the old city of Chiang Mai, in northern Thailand.

spots.name: Wat Suan Dok
spots.summary: Wat Suan Dok, also known as Wat Buppharam is a Buddhist temple (Wat) in Chiang Mai, northern Thailand. It is a Royal Temple of the Third Class. The temple is on Suthep Road, approximately one kilometre west of Suan Dok gate at the west side of the moat.

spots.name: Wat Lok Moli

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Lok Moli is a Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai, northern Thailand. The temple is situated on the north side of the north moat surrounding the old part of the city, about 400 meters west of the Chang Phuak city gate.

spots.name: Tha Phae Gate
spots.summary: Tha Phae Gate is the eastern and most famous gate of Chiang Mai, Thailand. It stands at the eastern side of the old walled city and today serves as a major landmark and public gathering place. The current structure is a reconstruction from 1985–1986, built on the site of the historic gate.

spots.name: Wat Umong
spots.summary: Wat Umong, or Wat Umong Suan Puthatham is a 700-year-old Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai, Thailand.

spots.name: Three Kings Monument
spots.summary: Three Kings Monument is a royal monument dedicated to Phaya Mangrai, Pho Khun Ramkhamhaeng, and Phaya Ngammueang, considered the founding fathers of Lanna Kingdom. It is located in the center of Chiang Mai and was designed and cast by national artist Kaimook Chuto to commemorate the founding of the city.

spots.name: Wat Phra That Doi Kham

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Phra That Doi Kham is a Buddhist temple in the Mae Hia sub-district, Chiang Mai, Thailand. Situated atop Doi Kham hill at an elevation of approximately 200 meters above sea level, the temple is a significant historical and religious site that enshrines relics of the Buddha. Its original name was Wat Suwannabanpot.

spots.name: Wat Sri Suphan

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Sri Suphan is a Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai, northern Thailand. It is situated on Wualai Road, Haiya district, in the southern part of the old city. It is known as the "Silver Temple" because its ordination hall was constructed using silver, aluminium and nickel.

spots.name: Wiang Kum Kam

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wiang Kum Kam is an historic settlement and archaeological site along the Ping River, which was built by King Mangrai the Great as his capital before he moved it to Chiang Mai.

spots.name: Wat Mahawan

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Mahawan is a Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai, Thailand. It is located on the eastern periphery of the old city of Chiang Mai in Thaphae Road.

spots.name: Wat Phan Tao

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Phan Tao is a Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai, northern Thailand. It is situated on Prapokklao Road, Mueang Chiang Mai district, in the centre of the old city.

spots.name: Wat Buppharam

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Buppharam is a Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai, Thailand. Founded in 1497 by King Kaew, the temple was where Kawila began a ritual circumambulation of Chiang Mai to reoccupy it after two centuries of Burmese rule. Most of the temple buildings date to the late 1800s.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Ket Karam or Wat Sa Ket is a Buddhist temple (Wat) in Chiang Mai, Thailand

spots.name: Ban Ho Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Hedaytul Islam Mosque, near the Chiang Mai Night Bazaar, is one of the biggest mosques in the province, and also one of the seven mosques in Chiang Mai, Thailand, founded by Chinese migrants.

spots.name: Wat Chiang Yuen

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Chiang Yuen is a Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai, Thailand, located just north of the walled city, outside the Chang Phueak Gate. The temple name Chiang Yuen consists of two words: chiang and yuen, together meaning the temple of "the city that stands ".

spots.name: Wat Prasat

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Prasat is a Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai, northern Thailand. It is situated on Inthawarorot Road in the old city.

spots.name: Wat Chedi Liam

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Chedi Liam, formerly known as Wat Ku Kham, is one of the wats in the ancient Thai city of Wiang Kum Kam, now part of present-day Chiang Mai.

spots.name: Wat Umong Maha Thera Chan

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Umong Maha Thera Chan is a Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai, northern Thailand. It is situated on Ratchapakhinai Road in the centre of the old city.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Duang Di is a Buddhist temple located in the old city of Chiang Mai, northern Thailand.

spots.name: Wat Pan Sao

spots.summary: Wat Pan Sao is a temple under the Mahanikaya sect of Buddhism, located in Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai district, Chiang Mai.

spots.name: Wat Saen Fang

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Saen Fang is a Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai, Thailand. The temple was founded in the 1500s, but all extant structures date to the 1800s or later. The viharn of Wat Saen Fang previously served as the royal residence of Kawirolot in the 1860s, and was converted into a viharn by his successor, Inthawichayanon in 1878.

spots.summary: Wat Mo Kham Tuang is a Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai, northern Thailand. It is situated in the old city overlooking the north side of the moat which surrounds the city.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Chang Kham, formerly known as Wat Kan Thom after the name of its builder, is a ruined temple that is part of the Wiang Kum Kam archaeological area, outside of Chiang Mai in northern Thailand. The present name of the temple is derived from elephant figures supporting one of the structures.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Chai Phrakiat, also known as Wat Chai Pha Kiat, is a Buddhist temple in Si Phum, Mueang Chiang Mai district, Chiang Mai province, Thailand. It is located within the historic walled city of Chiang Mai and belongs to the Maha Nikaya order.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Khuan Khama, also known as the Golden Horse Temple, is a Buddhist temple located within the old city walls of Chiang Mai, Thailand. Situated on Sri Poom Road near the Chang Phuak Gate, the temple is known for its distinctive golden horse statues.

spots.name: Wat Lam Chang

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Lam Chang is a Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai, northern Thailand. Situated in the old city, the temple was established at the beginning of the 14th century by King Mangrai, the first king of Lan Na (1296–1311) and founder of Chiang Mai.

spots.name: Wat Dok Kham

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Dok Kham is a Buddhist temple in Si Phum, Mueang Chiang Mai district, Chiang Mai province, Thailand, located on Mun Mueang Road near Tha Phae Gate. It is traditionally dated to 1783, during the reign of Kawila, and has a Lanna-style vihara and chedi.

spots.name: Wat Chang Taem

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Chang Taem is a Buddhist temple in Phra Sing, Mueang Chiang Mai district, Chiang Mai province, Thailand. It is located on Phra Pok Klao Road in Chiang Mai.

spots.summary: Wat Chang Khong is a Buddhist temple in Chang Khlan, Mueang Chiang Mai district, Chiang Mai province, Thailand. It is associated with a community of gong makers, from which the temple takes its name.

spots.name: Wat I Khang
spots.summary: Wat I Khang is a ruined 16th or 17th century temple in the Wiang Kum Kam archaeological complex near modern Chiang Mai in northern Thailand.

spots.name: Wat Chai Si Phum

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wat Chai Si Phum, also known as Wat Phan Ta Koen, is a Buddhist temple in Mueang Chiang Mai district, Chiang Mai province, Thailand. It stands near Si Phum Corner, at the northeastern corner of the old city of Chiang Mai, near the former city moat.

spots.name: Wat Pu Pia
spots.summary: Wat Pu Pia is a semi ruined temple in the Wiang Kum Kam archaeological complex, outside of modern Chiang Mai in northern Thailand. It is notable within the archaeological area inside Wiang Kum Kam for its relatively good state of preservation, including some remnants of stucco work and an intact layout.

spots.name: Wat That Noi
spots.summary: Wat That Noi is a ruined temple of the Wiang Kum Kam archaeological area, outside of Chiang Mai in northern Thailand, so named because of its relatively restricted scale.

spots.name: Lanna Architecture Center
spots.summary: Located in the Khum Chao Burirat Mahain Building, a two storey house as an example of the western influence on native architecture in early Chiang Mai times, there are videos, photos, and models about traditional Thai buildings. You can also buy postcards, pencils, and tees about Khum Chao Burirat there. There are several stamps of Thai building pictures to stamp on your booklet.

spots.name: The Treasury Museum Chiang Mai
spots.summary: One of two money museums in Thailand, focused on northern Thailand, run by government treasury department, in a heritage building. It is small: plan 1 hr to see, need to take off shoes.

spots.name: Ben Cocktail Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A tiny, hole-in-the-wall (~15 seat) cocktail bar that just may serve the best cocktails in Chiang Mai. Certainly the best price/performance. Run by Ben, an irrepressible, animal-loving, lovely female and her partner, Keng. She is especially proud of her mojitos, but all the 270 cocktails on offer are delicious. The conversation is good too as she speaks excellent English. Free Wi-Fi. Great place t

spots.name: Deaf Shop

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A small vinyl listening bar with a cozy atmosphere that seems to serve as a shop during the day. At night a curated selection of LPs and hosts events with guest DJs makes it a unique spot for music lovers in the city. It fits only a tiny crowd of about 30–50 people, so don't come too late! After midnight they will close the front gate to continue raving — don't worry, this is not a scheme to disto

spots.name: Number 1 Bistro/Cafe
spots.summary: Great expat bar. Free Wi-Fi with electrical outlets spaced at one metre intervals under the bar. They specialise in Belgian beer as well as having eight draught beers on tap, including domestic and Guinness. Excellent kitchen serving Thai and farang food, although the latter can be pricy: pad Thai is 80 baht, while the cheeseburger is expensive at 250 baht (July 2015). Number 1 is a refuge in Chia

spots.name: The North Gate Jazz Collective

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Nightly jazz performances starting around 21:30 with different performers and occasional guests from the audience. A surprisingly young crowd for the type of music they play here. If you are a music enthusiast, the performance can be a mixed bag: sometimes great, sometimes mediocre. However, the range of available stimulants in Chiang Mai will ensure that you will have a great time, especially if

spots.name: Tien Sieng Vegetarian Foods
spots.summary: Delicious vegan buffet. There are a few great dishes: the tofu, mushroom, and lemon grass wrapped in banana leaves is addictive; the het-hom (shitake) and other protein/gluten goodies are lovely; the steaming noodle soup is a great addition to a meal if you've arrived late and want to warm up the buffet dishes. The earlier the better as when dishes run out, they aren't remade. Also, you can buy so

spots.name: V T Namneung

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Handsome 2-storey restaurant with air-con upstairs. Serves what amounts to Vietnamese tapas: spring rolls, salted pork ribs, nem; all with lots of leafy greens. Serve beer, but the fresh fruit juices are better. Do very little to cater to visitors as most everything is in Thai including signs and menus. At the entry have a shop that offers many of their products packaged for take-away. The website

spots.name: Chiang Mai Cabaret Show
spots.summary: A nightly revue, dancing to Western tunes by ladyboys in lavish costumes. The one hour show is tame and family-friendly, with children frequently in the audience. Lots of dancing to ABBA tunes and extravagant costumes, with no nudity. The show's length is perfect and the price is surprising affordable. Good fun. Happy Hour precedes the show, 19:30-20:30, and also follows the show.

spots.name: O'Malley's Irish Pub
spots.summary: Delicious cocktails and excellent Western and Thai food. Has inside (air conditioned) and outside (smoking) seating. The interior closely resembles an authentic pub. This place does all the small things well: Tabasco, Lea & Perrins on the tables, soap and towels in the toilets, spotlessly clean. Not cheap, but the food is superb and the portions generous. Free Wi-Fi.

spots.name: Blow

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A small bar with young crowd. Small scale drag show on Thursday and Saturday from 22:15 to 23:30 approximately (sometimes it started later if queens arrived later). No entrance fee for drag shows. The show stage is simply space between tables on two side, and one staff will stand near the entrance door holding a flashlight for lightning.

spots.name: Red CNX

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A western orientated club known for its energetic atmosphere with famous host DJs from time to time and electronic music genres like House and Techno. Young and hip. Due to its size (more than 150 people), it will need a decent crowd to be fun. Don't pay entrance if you are not 100% sure that there is a crowd inside, ready to let loose.

spots.name: The Red Lion English Pub
spots.summary: Draught Guinness and Heineken, imported Blackthorn Cider and Fuller's London Pride, and Belgian and German beers. Pub favourites including bangers 'n mash, fish 'n chips, steak & kidney pie as well as steaks, pasta and Thai food. Live sports on a HD big screen including Premier League Football, Aussie Rules, Rugby and Formula 1.

spots.name: The Good View
spots.summary: Thai and Western varieties of rock, jazz, pop and country music in the evening. Their extensive menu offers more than 150 Thai, Chinese, and Western dishes, including curries, noodles, rice and pizza. Full-service bar serving wine, beer and spirits. If you want to get in, get there early and there's a queue every night.

spots.name: Fuji

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: While perhaps not a special restaurant in that it is not unique to Chiang Mai (it's actually a large chain), for those seeking reasonably-priced Japanese food, Fuji is a must. There are several spectacular set meals that offer superb value, e.g., the Fuji Sashimi Set which can easily fill up a sushi lover

spots.name: Ming Kwan Vegetarian Buffet
spots.summary: A different range of Thai vegan dishes from the norm. A focus on faux-meats, the veggie sausage is great, and the faux-fish in curry sauce is good. Of course, bamboo shoot stir fry, noodle soups, etc., means there's lots to try. They cook during the day, so other dishes often appear from the kitchen.

spots.name: Norden Restaurant Chiang Mai
spots.summary: A modern European restaurant with our roots & inspiration from Scandinavia all cooked from a Swedish chef & owner. Then menu has many steaks, BBQ ribs, Pizza, and Nordic Food. The quality of the food is outstanding without the price tag to go with it. Very reasonably priced.

spots.name: Chiangmai Saloon

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: American-style burger and steakhouse. Friendly staff, nice atmosphere, music videos and sports on three 3-m screens, pool tables and free Internet, free popcorn and peanuts, over 50 kinds of margaritas, Chang beer on tap. Is open everyday from breakfast until late.

spots.name: The Duke's Ping River
spots.summary: Excellent American-style dishes and desserts: ribs, burgers, pizza, cheesecake, etc. Full bar with local and imported beers and wines. Great family atmosphere, children's menu, no loud music or entertainment, just good food. Eat in, take away & call for delivery.

spots.name: Lim Lao Ngow Fishball Noodle
spots.summary: Egg noodle and fishballs. Besides common egg noodle, they also offer a flat shape egg node using double proportion of eggs and Hong Kong style flour. Their original branch in Yaowarach (China Town in Bangkok) was listed as Bib Gourmand in Michaelin Guide Bangko.

spots.name: Dash! Restaurant & Bar
spots.summary: Possibly the best value in Chiang Mai. Wonderful ambiance, with indoor or outdoor seating. Great food, cocktails and desserts at more than reasonable prices. Cooking classes offered on-site. Also has a 3-bedroom, 2-bath house for rent at 3,000 baht per day.

spots.name: Vegan Heaven
spots.summary: A 100% vegan restaurant in the tourist area of Chiang Mai. It has a wide variety of meals: the usual Thai dishes in vegan, such as khao soi, tom yam, tom kha and pad see ew, but also breakfast meals, sandwiches and even vegan hot dogs and burgers.
